scope: Bounded adversarial expectations review as of November 4, 2026. Public sources only; no account creation, paid access, model changes, target fitting, or winning probability.

verdict.preferred_research_counterclaim: Intel: even successful CPU and packaging growth may fail to deliver the owner cash implied by a recovery valuation because qualified capacity, replacement, substrates, and partner economics require persistently more capital than bulls assume.
verdict.what_would_make_it_differentiated: Quantify a specific, same-scope disagreement about 2028-2031 capital productivity and parent cash conversion against an identified current professional forecast. High 2027 capex, negative 2027 free cash flow, and late foundry profitability are already public expectations.
verdict.direction_supported_now: This source review does not independently establish an attractive 3-5 year Intel short. It identifies a testable counterclaim, but does not identify a reliable market-wide mature capital assumption and prove it too optimistic. The supplied existing model outputs must govern the conditional return discussion; public targets cannot be used to fit assumptions.
verdict.spacex_comparison: SpaceX's generic normalization argument is already explicit in Morningstar. Differentiation would require a specific forecast of qualified, paid capacity, repeat pricing and procurement economics, with a stock-return bridge. The gas/power work cannot establish those commercial outcomes. New post-Q3 individual forecasts make a stale pre-Q3 consensus comparison inadequate.
verdict.competition_fit: A valuation gap today is not automatically a profitable 3-5 year short. The dated exit value, evolution of operating expectations, financing claims, and short carrying economics must be consistent. There is no invented mandatory catalyst rule.

prominent_source_quality_warning.conflict: Its public table gives FY2026 revenue of $56.2763B, while the same page's narrative says 2026 will finish near $61.7B and discusses a $15.5B Q4 guidance midpoint.
prominent_source_quality_warning.consequence: Do not use its FY2027/FY2028 numbers as a hard consensus mismatch or as a fully reconciled professional operating model. They are one publisher's displayed estimates with an unresolved internal inconsistency. This review does not determine whether the table or narrative is stale.
prominent_source_quality_warning.further_limit: The full cash-flow workbook requires an account. No workbook or long-term capital assumptions were verified.

verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Fair value cut from $105 to $85; no moat; very high uncertainty. The article acknowledges PC weakness and server/substrate constraints while describing shares as modestly undervalued at publication.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: One firm's contemporaneous valuation, not consensus or a dated 2030 target. No explicit long-term capex schedule is disclosed in the reviewed article.

verified_publisher_expectations.published: 2026-10-30 rating change recorded on publisher's superseded preview
verified_publisher_expectations.facts: The publisher explicitly marks the $175 preview superseded and records its October 30 Hold rating and $80 target.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: The successor page was inaccessible in this review. The old bullish target and preview forecasts are not current expectations; no successor capital schedule was verified.

verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Hold. The analysis already treats higher 2027 spending and unlikely positive 2027 free cash flow as recognized risks.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: Single publisher, not consensus. The table/narrative inconsistency above prevents a hard numerical expectations claim.

verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Moorhead places foundry profitability around 2029 or 2030 and discusses negative free cash flow from heavy investment.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: The article identifies itself as an AI-generated, human-edited summary of his broadcast. It is an industry analyst's outlook, not an equity consensus model or quantified long-term capex schedule.

verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Maintains Outperform and gives a $144-$191 fair-value range. Already discusses the larger capital bill and debt funding.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: Post-Q3, but one publisher rather than consensus. SI includes more than rental revenue. The root's supplied $334.607B 2028 rental figure exceeds this publisher's entire SI forecast, but this is a scope-validation flag, not proof of a market-wide mismatch or a reason to fit the model.

verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Raises fair value to $70 from $62 while explicitly questioning indefinite scarcity and long-term AI infrastructure returns.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: Direct-publisher search text was available; opening the full page returned 403. Its thesis already contains the generic lower-rent argument. Its present fair value is not comparable to the project's conditional end-2030 share value without a dated bridge.

verified_publisher_expectations.publisher: S&P Global Market Intelligence / Visible Alpha
verified_publisher_expectations.facts: Explicit pre-Q3 consensus preview. It already discusses rising capex, debt, and uncertainty over infrastructure returns.
verified_publisher_expectations.limit: No verified public post-Q3 Visible Alpha replacement was located. This dated preview cannot represent November 4 consensus.

additional_capital_search_result.visible_assumptions: The page assumes $26B in 2027, $25B annually in 2028-2029, and about $22.7B annually in 2030-2031 for listed capital programs.
additional_capital_search_result.exclusion_reason: It still labels Q3 2026 projected, no reliable current publication/update date was found, professional research provenance was not established, and the page says these amounts are assumptions. Its program/table methodology and cash denominator have not been reconciled. Excluded from professional-consensus comparisons.

intel_tests: Reconcile successive filings' cash property purchases, deferred equipment payments, lease cash, incentives, supplier prepayments, customer deposits, and partner contributions/distributions. Keep gross capital spending separate from parent cash burden.

Track qualified node output, loading, process-cost improvement, and recurring external revenue against the physical additions required to produce them. Internal foundry transfers must eliminate in consolidated revenue.
Separate premium CPU mix from same-product pricing and units, then test whether product and packaging growth improves parent cash after replacement and working capital.
Read customer capacity commitments for actual funding, qualification timing, and obligations. Missing public customer names alone do not prove missing demand.
spacex_tests: Compare realized paid external capacity, renewal/backfill pricing and service qualification with procurement and replacement cash on consistent units.
Use post-Q3 dated professional forecasts for an expectations comparison; distinguish annual revenue from exit run rate and rental revenue from total AI revenue.
Treat near-term physical activity as a delivery check, not as evidence of durable paid occupancy or a mature rental premium.
public_evidence_that_could_validate_the_.status: These are validation paths, not findings that the proposed short counterclaim has been proved.
